newsitem.title: USA: Russian PGM exports still seen in 3 weeks - Almaz.
newsitem.headline: Russian PGM exports still seen in 3 weeks - Almaz.

text.p: Russian exports of platinum group metals are still expected to resume in late June after a suspension since last December, a spokesman for the U.S. branch of Russian metals export agency Almaz said Thursday.
"The situation is little changed from a week ago," Almaz USA spokesman Max Belov told Reuters.
"We are still awaiting the finalization of some paperwork on the export licences and officials are going to Japan this weekend to negotiate export sales of platinum and palladium," he said.

Russian exports of platinum and palladium have been suspended since December 1996 due to Russian fiscal and administrative problems. However, some analysts suspect Russia changed its marketing policy in an attempt to conserve its stockpiles and push prices up.

Platinum and palladium prices have risen sharly this year, with platinum fixed in London Thursday at $417.40 an ounce, its highest since Feb 21, 1996, while palladium was fixed at an all-time high of $196.50.
"The size of the export quotas remains secret, but as we are now nearly half way through the year, obviously Russian exports are likely to be less than last year," Belov said.

"Sometimes in past years the government has added to the quotas during the year, but things have changed administratively this year with the central bank now more in control of the stockpile," he said.
Russia supplies about 60 percent of the world's palladium and about 20 percent of its platinum.
